column1: # Provisional game profile of Chained Echoes (Switch, base game v0 + update v1310720 + the Ashes of Elrant DLC), Unity 2020.3.36f1 IL2CPP, SDK 14.3.0, NVN. Written by Peanuts Native from a survey of
# the game files with dm/games/profile_guess.py; the game has not been booted with it. Every key marked "guess" follows a rule or a sibling profile and is not measured. README.md beside this file.
# guess: a 2D role-playing game moved with the stick or the D-pad; the 3D layout has the D-pad. Nothing in the files decides it
# The display version was not read (the import keeps no control data)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk0, sdk. subsdk0 is NintendoSDK_movie: main takes 25 functions from it (movie::Extractor, movie::Decoder: Unity's video player), none of which
# the file every Unity player has (as the other Unity profiles); profile_guess.py's rule would name the largest file, a music bundle
# the file types that are big or already compressed (profile_guess.py's rule)
# guess for this build, not measured here. The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so there is virtual address memory; main also imports nn::os::SetMemoryHeapSize. The 5 GB block
# (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region) with the hardware pool, as upstream nxnative's profile of update 1.1.1 (v131072), which played the
# prologue on the Mac with it: the alias region's high-water mark +3.5 GB of 64 GB, 1.95 GB resident. The sdk build (2aef2cff…) is the one that profile used, with the SDK-wide
# node area cut and 2 MB region alignment (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py). No heap check has run on either build
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----

# guess (Fire Emblem Engage's groups, the other Unity 2020.3 game with Addressables): engine built-ins (Resources/) go to engine, the Addressables bundles to assets, the player's serialized files to data
